prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Regional Dispatch Center (alias/call sign Juniper) provides continuous emergency medical request intake, triage support, ambulance dispatch, regional coordination, shared operational picture. Mandate: translate reports into prioritized incidents and coordinate response under approved clinical/jurisdictional protocols. Participating jurisdictions retain resource ownership/local policy responsibility; regional service coordinates agreed response. Operating area is divided into response zones; zone boundaries maintained with jurisdictions and reviewed after road network, population, or service agreement changes. Dispatch decisions must reflect distance, road access, travel time, road restrictions, weather, closures, and ambulance capacity. Each zone has primary/alternate routes to Emergency Department and Riverside Trauma Center, subject to clinical direction/current access. Crews verify rapidly changing access before constrained routes.

Actors/elements: Call Taker Mara uses Computer Aided Dispatch Console to collect details/location and enter assessment request. Triage Supervisor assigns/confirms priority and requests clinical review. Regional Medical Director sets clinical triage policy/limits; dispatch personnel must seek clinical guidance beyond delegated authority. Shift Commander (alias/call sign Sundial) is on-duty operational authority for coordination/service continuity, priorities during surges, conflict resolution, and escalation beyond center authority; does not replace Regional Medical Director policy authority or Paramedic Crew scene judgment. Radio Coordinator (alias/call sign Mistral) manages/monitors Regional Radio Network, maintains radio discipline/clear communications among dispatch personnel and ambulance crews, confirms assigned channels and backup procedures at shift start. Radio checks verify weak-signal coverage and equipment/network problems. Regional Radio Network carries authorized dispatch/coordination communications. Ambulance Coordination Platform shows incidents, assignments, regional resources. Paramedic Crew assesses/cares for patients. Ambulance Unit 417 is in regional pool when assigned. Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates awareness of receiving capacity/destination constraints; Emergency Department communicates receiving considerations; Riverside Trauma Center is designated destination.

Fleet Maintenance Cell (alias/call sign Bluejay) provides operational awareness, monitors vehicle availability, servicing, defects, maintenance constraints affecting zone coverage, and produces Battery Swap Voucher for authorized battery replacement. Data Quality Officer reviews dispatch records for completeness, consistency, information-handling compliance. Readiness checks confirm staffing, communications equipment, clinical supplies, fuel, vehicle condition, maintenance restrictions. North Gate Status Board presents northern access/queue conditions and produces North Approach Queue Snapshot. South Gate Status Board presents southern access/restrictions affecting ambulance entry. Both gate boards checked at shift start and on relevant access changes.

New part:
S044: The Ambulance Coordination Platform provides a shared operational view of zone coverage and unit availability.
S045: The Computer Aided Dispatch Console supports dispatch work, while operational staff remain responsible for verifying that displayed information is current.
S046: The Shift Commander reviews readiness concerns that may require repositioning resources or adjusting local coverage plans.
S047: The Triage Supervisor coordinates clinical prioritization with dispatch operations when demand or access conditions change.
S048: The Paramedic Crew reports new access barriers and vehicle readiness concerns through established communications procedures.
S049: The Regional Dispatch Center compares reported conditions with current zone coverage and escalates unresolved readiness gaps to the appropriate operational lead.
S050: Readiness status is reassessed after significant incidents, service interruptions, or changes to routes and access conditions.
S051: The Regional Dispatch Center handles incoming emergency calls through a controlled intake process that creates an incident record for coordination.
S052: Call Taker Mara is also known by the radio alias Larkspur.
S053: The Hospital Liaison Desk is also known by the coordination alias Kestrel.
S054: Call Taker Mara establishes the caller's location before collecting medical details.
S055: Call Taker Mara asks for the street address, municipality, and any building, floor, or entrance information needed to find the patient.
S056: Call Taker Mara confirms the location by repeating the address and checking it against the caller's description of nearby landmarks.
S057: Call Taker Mara asks whether the caller can provide a callback number in case the connection is lost.
S058: Call Taker Mara gathers the patient's age, level of consciousness, breathing status, and the main reason emergency help is needed.
S059: Call Taker Mara uses direct questions to distinguish observed symptoms from information reported by someone else.
S060: Call Taker Mara records the time symptoms began when the caller can provide a reliable estimate.
S061: Call Taker Mara notes access barriers such as locked entrances, restricted roads, or difficulty reaching the patient.
S062: Call Taker Mara produces the Caller Location Correction Slip when the caller's address needs documented clarification.
S063: The Computer Aided Dispatch Console checks entered location details against available address and map data.
S064: If the location does not resolve cleanly, Call Taker Mara asks focused follow-up questions and updates the incident record.
S065: Call Taker Mara remains engaged with the caller when further information could change the response priority or access plan.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
